chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Ubayd Allah ibn al-Marzuban, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام one year before he came to al-ʿIrāq, while ʿAlī, his son, was sitting before him. He looked at me and said, "O Muhammad, indeed there will be an upheaval in this year, so do not be distressed by that." He said: I said, "What will happen? May I be made your ransom, for what you mentioned has troubled me."
So he said, "I shall go to the tyrant. Indeed, no evil will begin from him toward me, but from the one who will be after him." He said: I said, "And what will happen? May I be made your ransom."
He said: "Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does whatever He wills."
He said: I said, "And what is that? May I be made your ransom."

He said, "Whoever wrongs this son of mine regarding his right, and denies his Imamate after me, is like one who wronged ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام in his right and denied his Imamate after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله." He said: I said, "By Allah, if Allah extends my life, I will surely submit to him his right and I will surely acknowledge his Imamate."

He said, "You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Allah will extend your life, and you will submit to him his right, acknowledge his Imamate, and the Imamate of the one who will come after him." He said: I said, "And who is that?" He said, "Muhammad, his son." He said: I said to him, "Acceptance and submission."

key_terms.إِمَامَتَهُ: his divinely designated Imamate and authority
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: submission and yielding in acknowledgment of divine authority
key_terms.الطَّاغِيَةِ: the tyrannical ruler to whom the Imam عليه السلام would be taken
key_terms.الظَّالِمِينَ: the wrongdoers whom Allah leaves astray
key_terms.حَرَكَةٌ: an upheaval or disturbance foretold to occur in that year
key_terms.حَقَّهُ: his rightful due and claim that must be acknowledged

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام indicate the Imamate of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام and the Imam after him?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام foretelling trials connected to his going to the ruler and affirming the Imamate of his son ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام, followed by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام. It presents denial of the Imam’s rightful authority as a grave injustice comparable to denying the right of Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ali and Ubeydullah Bin Al Marzuban, from Ibn Sinan who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> from before he<sup>asws</sup> had proceeded to Al-Iraq by a year, and Ali<sup>asws</sup>, his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> was seated in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at me and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad! There would be happening, during this year, a disturbance, therefore do not panic due to that’. I said, ‘And what would happen? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, as it has worried me, what you<sup>asws</sup> have mentioned’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall be going to the tyrant, it would begin for me<sup>asws</sup> evil from him and from the one who would happen to be after him’. I said, ‘And what would happen? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Lets to stray the unjust ones and He<sup>azwj</sup> Does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’.
I said, ‘And what is that? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who oppresses this son<sup>asws</sup> of mine<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>asws</sup> rights and rejects his<sup>asws</sup> Imamate after me<sup>asws</sup>, would be like the one who oppressed Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> of his<sup>asws</sup> right and rejected his<sup>asws</sup> Imamate after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’. I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> was to Extend for me regarding the life-span, I will submit to him<sup>asws</sup> his<sup>asws</sup> right and I will acknowledge to him<sup>asws</sup> with his<sup>asws</sup> Imamate’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You speak the truth, O Muhammad! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Extend in your life-span and you will submit to him<sup>asws</sup> his<sup>asws</sup> right and accept to him<sup>asws</sup> with his<sup>asws</sup> Imamate, and the Imamate of the one<sup>asws</sup> who would happen to be after him<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘And who is that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’. I said to him, ‘The agreement and the submission (from me)’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ali and ‘Abdallah ibn al-Marzuban from (Muhammad) ibn Sinan who has said the following.

“Once I went to see abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) one year before he would leave for Iraq. His son Ali (a.s.) was also in the meeting. He looked at me and said, “O Muhammad, during this year a movement will take place do not be disturbed in it.”

The narrator has said that he then asked the Imam (a.s.), “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what that will be? What you said has made me very anxious.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “I will journey to the tyrant. From his and one after him I will not suffer any serious harm.” The narrator has said that he then asked The Imam (a.s.), “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what then will happen?”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “ Allah causes the unjust to go astray and He does whatever He wills.”
The narrator has said that he then asked the Imam (a.s.), “‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what is that will happen?”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “Whoever will do injustice to my son this one, reject his Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) after me it would like doing injustice to Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) and reject his Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) after the Messenger of Allah.” The narrator has said that he then asked The Imam (a.s.), “By Allah, if Allah will grant me long life I will acknowledge his right and will affirm his Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority).”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Allah will grant you long life.You will acknowledge his right and affirm his Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) and the Imamat of the one after him.” The narrator has said that he then asked The Imam (a.s.), “Who will he be?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Muhammad, his son.” The narrator has said that he then asked The Imam (a.s.), “From me it is agreed and accepted.”
